steps: The 1987 Constitution is the supreme (highest) law of the Philippines.
Every other law, ordinance or government act must agree with it. If a law goes against the Constitution, the courts can strike it down as unconstitutional.
Think of it as the master rulebook: it creates the government, divides its powers, and lists the rights of the people.
Words like "supreme law", "fundamental law" or "highest law of the land" in a question point to the Constitution.

wrong.Civil Code: The Civil Code covers private matters like family, property and contracts. It is an ordinary law and must follow the Constitution.
wrong.Revised Penal Code: The Revised Penal Code defines crimes and their penalties. It is an ordinary law below the Constitution.
wrong.Local Government Code: The Local Government Code (RA 7160) governs provinces, cities, municipalities and barangays. It is an ordinary law below the Constitution.

89.tip: Constitution on top; all other laws must bow to it.

steps: RA 6713 is the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees, passed in 1989.
It tells government workers how to behave: the eight norms of conduct, duties like answering letters promptly, prohibited acts like accepting gifts, and filing the SALN.
Its goal is honest, simple and efficient public service, because government workers are paid by the people.
If a question mentions norms of conduct, simple living, SALN or political neutrality, think RA 6713.

wrong.Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act: That is RA 3019 (1960), which lists corrupt acts of public officers.
wrong.Ease of Doing Business Act: That is RA 11032 (2018), which speeds up government transactions and created the Anti-Red Tape Authority.
wrong.Civil Service Law: The Civil Service Law is a separate body of rules on hiring, promotion and discipline in government. It is not RA 6713.

90.tip: 6713 = Code of Conduct: "how to act" as a public servant.

steps: "Public office is a public trust" is the opening line of Article XI, Section 1, titled Accountability of Public Officers.
It means a government position is not personal property. It is entrusted by the people, so officials must serve with responsibility, integrity, loyalty and efficiency.
Article XI also covers impeachment and the Ombudsman, all tools for keeping officials accountable.
Accountability, impeachment, Ombudsman, public trust: all are in Article XI.

wrong.Article II: Article II is the Declaration of Principles and State Policies (for example, sovereignty resides in the people).
wrong.Article III: Article III is the Bill of Rights.
wrong.Article IX: Article IX covers the Constitutional Commissions: CSC, COMELEC and COA.

steps: RA 11032 is the Ease of Doing Business and Efficient Government Service Delivery Act of 2018.
It amended the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007 (RA 9485) to make government transactions faster and simpler.
It set processing deadlines (3, 7 and 20 working days) and created the Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA).
If a question mentions ease of doing business, ARTA or red tape after 2018, the answer is RA 11032.

wrong.RA 9485: RA 9485 is the older Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007, which RA 11032 amended.
wrong.RA 10173: RA 10173 is the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
wrong.RA 9184: RA 9184 is the Government Procurement Reform Act, about how government buys goods and services.

92.tip: Ease of Doing Business 2018 = RA 11032 (the newest number, the newest law).

steps: Under RA 11032, a simple transaction must be finished within 3 working days.
The full set: simple = 3 working days, complex = 7 working days, highly technical = 20 working days.
This exists so citizens are not kept waiting for weeks for simple papers like certificates.
Working days do not count weekends and holidays.

wrong.1 working day: There is no 1-day maximum for simple transactions under RA 11032.
wrong.7 working days: 7 working days is the limit for complex transactions.
wrong.20 working days: 20 working days is the limit for highly technical applications.

steps: RA 9003 is the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000.
It deals with garbage: segregation at source, recycling, composting, Materials Recovery Facilities, and banning open dumps.
It makes LGUs, especially barangays, responsible for managing waste.

wrong.RA 8749: RA 8749 is the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999.
wrong.RA 9275: RA 9275 is the Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004, not solid waste.
wrong.RA 9729: RA 9729 is the Climate Change Act of 2009.

steps: RA 8749 is the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999.
It aims to reduce air pollution from vehicles, factories and burning.
It bans incineration of waste that gives off poisonous and toxic fumes.

wrong.RA 9003: RA 9003 is the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000.
wrong.RA 9275: RA 9275 is the Philippine Clean Water Act of 2004.
wrong.RA 7160: RA 7160 is the Local Government Code of 1991.

95.tip: Air came first (1999, RA 8749), then garbage (2000, RA 9003), then water (2004, RA 9275).

steps: A Senator serves a term of 6 years (Article VI, Section 4).
A Senator cannot serve more than two consecutive terms, so 12 straight years at most.
The longer term (compared to 3 years for House members) gives the Senate more stability and a national view.

wrong.3 years: 3 years is the term of a Member of the House of Representatives.
wrong.4 years: No national elective office in the 1987 Constitution has a 4-year term.
wrong.9 years: There is no 9-year term for Senators.

steps: The Senate has 24 Senators (Article VI, Section 2).
They are elected at large, meaning voters from the whole country vote for them, not just one district.
Because of staggered terms, about half (12) are elected every three years.

wrong.12: 12 is the number of Senators elected in each regular election, not the total.
wrong.30: The Senate does not have 30 members.
wrong.36: The Senate does not have 36 members.

steps: Article IX creates only three Constitutional Commissions: the Civil Service Commission (CSC), the Commission on Elections (COMELEC) and the Commission on Audit (COA).
The Commission on Human Rights (CHR) is created in a different article, Article XIII (Social Justice and Human Rights).
So CHR is a constitutional body, but it is not one of the three Constitutional Commissions.

wrong.Civil Service Commission: The CSC is a Constitutional Commission under Article IX-B.
wrong.Commission on Elections: COMELEC is a Constitutional Commission under Article IX-C.
wrong.Commission on Audit: COA is a Constitutional Commission under Article IX-D.

98.tip: Article IX: B-C-D = CSC, COMELEC, COA. CHR lives in XIII.

steps: A candidate for President must be at least 40 years old on the day of the election (Article VII, Section 2).
Other requirements: natural-born citizen, registered voter, able to read and write, and a resident of the Philippines for at least 10 years before the election.
The higher age is meant to ensure maturity and experience for the highest office.

wrong.35: 35 is the minimum age for a Senator.
wrong.45: 45 is not a constitutional age requirement for President.
wrong.50: 50 is not a constitutional age requirement for President.

steps: The Bill of Rights is Article III of the 1987 Constitution.
It protects people from abuse by the government: due process, free speech, freedom of religion, privacy, rights of the accused, and more.
These rights limit what the government can do to you.

wrong.Article II: Article II is the Declaration of Principles and State Policies.

100.tip: I Territory, II Principles, III Rights, IV Citizenship.

steps: Under RA 6713, public officials and employees file their SALN every year on or before April 30.
SALN means Statement of Assets, Liabilities and Net Worth: a list of what you own, what you owe, and your net worth.
It exists so the public can check if an official's wealth suddenly grows beyond their salary, which may signal corruption.

wrong.January 31: January 31 is not the SALN deadline under RA 6713.
wrong.June 30: June 30 is not the SALN deadline under RA 6713.
wrong.December 31: December 31 is the cut-off date of what you report in the SALN, but the filing deadline is April 30.

101.tip: SALN due in April, every year.

steps: The UN General Assembly adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948, in Paris.
It was written after World War II so the horrors of that war would never happen again.
December 10 is now celebrated as Human Rights Day.

wrong.1945: 1945 is the year the United Nations was founded.
wrong.1966: 1966 is the year the two International Covenants (on civil and political rights, and on economic, social and cultural rights) were adopted.
wrong.1986: 1986 is the year of the EDSA People Power Revolution in the Philippines.

102.tip: UN 1945, UDHR 1948, Human Rights Day December 10.

steps: RA 9729 is the Climate Change Act of 2009.
It made climate change part of government planning and created the Climate Change Commission.
Climate change = RA 9729; disaster risk reduction = RA 10121.

wrong.RA 10121: RA 10121 is the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010.
wrong.RA 9003: RA 9003 is the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000.
wrong.RA 8749: RA 8749 is the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999.

steps: The President serves a single term of 6 years and is not eligible for any reelection (Article VII, Section 4).
This rule came from history: the framers wanted to stop any President from staying in power for too long, as happened during martial law.
With no reelection, the President also does not need to use the office to campaign for another term.

wrong.4 years, one reelection: This describes the US system, not the Philippines.
wrong.6 years, one reelection: The term is 6 years, but the President cannot be reelected at all.

steps: RA 10173 is the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
It protects personal information (like your name, address and ID numbers) collected by government and private companies.
It created the National Privacy Commission to enforce it.

wrong.RA 10175: RA 10175 is the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012, a different law from the same year.
wrong.RA 11032: RA 11032 is the Ease of Doing Business Act of 2018.
wrong.RA 9485: RA 9485 is the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007.

steps: A Senator must be at least 35 years old on election day (Article VI, Section 3).
Other requirements: natural-born citizen, able to read and write, registered voter, and a resident of the Philippines for at least 2 years before the election.

wrong.25: 25 is the minimum age for a Member of the House of Representatives.
wrong.30: 30 is not a constitutional age requirement for Senator.
wrong.40: 40 is the minimum age for President and Vice President.

steps: RA 7160 is the Local Government Code of 1991.
It gives provinces, cities, municipalities and barangays more power and resources to govern themselves (decentralization).
Questions about LGU powers, barangay officials or local taxes usually point to RA 7160.

wrong.RA 6713: RA 6713 is the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.
wrong.RA 9485: RA 9485 is the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007.
wrong.RA 8749: RA 8749 is the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999.

steps: The sun on the Philippine flag has 8 rays.
They stand for the first eight provinces that rose against Spain: Manila, Cavite, Bulacan, Pampanga, Nueva Ecija, Bataan, Laguna and Batangas.
The three stars stand for Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao.

wrong.5: The sun does not have 5 rays.
wrong.7: The sun does not have 7 rays.
wrong.12: The sun does not have 12 rays.

steps: In 2015 the UN adopted 17 Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) as part of the 2030 Agenda.
They include ending poverty and hunger, quality education, gender equality, clean water, climate action and more.
They replaced the 8 Millennium Development Goals (MDGs).

wrong.8: 8 is the number of the older Millennium Development Goals, not the SDGs.

steps: RA 9710 is the Magna Carta of Women, passed in 2009.
It is a broad women's rights law that removes discrimination against women in all areas of life.
"Magna Carta" is Latin for "great charter", a big list of rights.

wrong.RA 7877: RA 7877 is the Anti-Sexual Harassment Act of 1995.
wrong.RA 9262: RA 9262 is the Anti-Violence Against Women and Their Children Act of 2004.
wrong.RA 11313: RA 11313 is the Safe Spaces Act of 2019.

steps: RA 11313 is the Safe Spaces Act of 2019, also called the Bawal Bastos Law.
It punishes gender-based sexual harassment in streets, public places, online, workplaces and schools, like catcalling and unwanted comments.
It covers more places than the older Anti-Sexual Harassment Act, which focused on work and school.

wrong.RA 7877: RA 7877 is the older Anti-Sexual Harassment Act of 1995.
wrong.RA 10173: RA 10173 is the Data Privacy Act of 2012.
wrong.RA 9710: RA 9710 is the Magna Carta of Women.

steps: Inalienable means something cannot be taken away or given up.
Human rights belong to you because you are human. Nobody can sell them, and you cannot surrender them.
A right may be limited in some lawful cases, but the person never stops owning it.

wrong.Universal: Universal means human rights belong to everyone everywhere.
wrong.Indivisible: Indivisible means all rights are equally important and cannot be separated.
wrong.Relative: Relative is not a characteristic of human rights.

112.tip: In-ALIEN-able: cannot be made someone else's.

steps: RA 10121 is the Philippine Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010.
It focuses on preparing for disasters before they happen, not just responding after.
It created the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Council (NDRRMC).

wrong.RA 9729: RA 9729 is the Climate Change Act of 2009.
wrong.RA 9003: RA 9003 is the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000.
wrong.RA 7160: RA 7160 is the Local Government Code of 1991.

steps: Article XIV, Section 6 says the national language of the Philippines is Filipino.
Filipino is meant to grow and be enriched by existing Philippine and other languages, not just one language.

wrong.Tagalog: Tagalog is a regional language and the main base of Filipino, but it is not the name of the national language.
wrong.English: English is an official language, not the national language.
wrong.Pilipino: Pilipino was an older name for the national language before the 1987 Constitution.

218.tip: National language: Filipino with an F.

steps: Article XIV, Section 7: the official languages are Filipino and, until otherwise provided by law, English.
This means both are used in government and schools, but Congress could change the status of English by law.
Regional languages are auxiliary (helping) official languages in their regions.

wrong.Filipino only: English is also an official language.
wrong.English only: Filipino is also an official language, and it is the national language.
wrong.Filipino, English and Spanish: Spanish is not an official language; the Constitution only promotes Spanish and Arabic on a voluntary and optional basis.

steps: A Member of the House of Representatives serves 3 years (Article VI, Section 7).
They cannot serve more than three consecutive terms, so 9 straight years at most.
Shorter terms keep district representatives close and answerable to their voters.

wrong.2 years: 2 years is the US House term, not the Philippines.
wrong.4 years: No national elective office here has a 4-year term.
wrong.6 years: 6 years is the term of a Senator and of the President.

steps: The President may declare martial law or suspend the privilege of the writ of habeas corpus for not more than 60 days (Article VII, Section 18).
The President must report to Congress within 48 hours. Congress may revoke it or extend it.
The limit exists because of the long martial law period before 1986: the framers wanted strict checks.

wrong.30 days: 30 days is the period within which the Supreme Court must decide a case questioning martial law, not its length.
wrong.90 days: 90 days is not the constitutional limit.
wrong.6 months: 6 months is far beyond the 60-day limit.

221.tip: Martial law: 60 days, report in 48 hours.

steps: Only Congress can declare the existence of a state of war (Article VI, Section 23).
It needs a two-thirds vote of both Houses in joint session, voting separately.
War affects the whole nation, so the decision belongs to the people's representatives, not one person.

wrong.The President: The President is Commander-in-Chief and commands the armed forces, but cannot declare war.
wrong.The Supreme Court: The Supreme Court decides cases; it has no power to declare war.
wrong.The Armed Forces: The Armed Forces follow civilian authority and cannot declare war.

222.tip: Congress declares war; the President commands the troops.

steps: A Member of the House must be at least 25 years old on election day (Article VI, Section 6).
Other requirements: natural-born citizen, able to read and write, registered voter in the district, and a resident there for at least 1 year (except party-list representatives).

wrong.21: 21 is not the age requirement for the House.
wrong.30: 30 is not the age requirement for the House.
wrong.35: 35 is the minimum age for a Senator.

steps: The CSC Chairman and Commissioners serve 7 years without reappointment (Article IX-B, Section 1).
COMELEC and COA members have the same 7-year rule.
No reappointment protects independence: they do not need to please anyone to keep their job.

wrong.5 years, with reappointment: There is no 5-year term, and reappointment is not allowed.

224.tip: Constitutional Commissions: lucky 7, one time only.

steps: RA 3019 is the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act, passed in 1960.
It lists corrupt acts of public officers, like asking for money in exchange for a government favor.
It is one of the oldest anti-corruption laws still in use.

wrong.RA 6713: RA 6713 is the Code of Conduct and Ethical Standards for Public Officials and Employees.
wrong.RA 9485: RA 9485 is the Anti-Red Tape Act of 2007.

steps: Political partisanship is NOT a norm of RA 6713. The real norm is political neutrality.
Neutrality means serving everyone fairly regardless of their party.

The eight norms: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy, simple living.

wrong.Commitment to public interest: This is a real norm: put the public's interest above personal interest.
wrong.Justness and sincerity: This is a real norm: be fair, honest and sincere.
wrong.Simple living: This is a real norm: live modestly and avoid showing off wealth.

steps: RA 8371 is the Indigenous Peoples' Rights Act (IPRA) of 1997.
It protects the rights of indigenous peoples to their ancestral domains, culture and self-governance.
It created the National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP).

wrong.RA 7160: RA 7160 is the Local Government Code of 1991.
wrong.RA 9710: RA 9710 is the Magna Carta of Women.
wrong.RA 8749: RA 8749 is the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999.

steps: The 1987 Constitution was ratified by the people in a plebiscite on February 2, 1987.
Ratified means approved by the people through a vote, which made it take effect.
It was written after the 1986 EDSA People Power Revolution.

wrong.February 25, 1986: February 25, 1986 is the end of the EDSA People Power Revolution.
wrong.June 12, 1898: June 12, 1898 is the declaration of Philippine independence from Spain.
wrong.July 4, 1946: July 4, 1946 is when the US recognized Philippine independence.

steps: The 1987 Constitution has 18 articles plus a Preamble.
It starts with Article I (National Territory) and ends with Article XVIII (Transitory Provisions).

wrong.15: 15 is not the number of articles.
wrong.16: 16 is not the number of articles; Article XVI is General Provisions.
wrong.22: 22 is not the number of articles.

steps: This is Article II, Section 1 (Declaration of Principles and State Policies).
The full line: the Philippines is a democratic and republican State; sovereignty resides in the people and all government authority emanates from them.
It means the people are the true source of power. Officials only borrow that power.

wrong.Article III: Article III is the Bill of Rights.
wrong.Article VI: Article VI is the Legislative Department.

349.tip: Article II = basic principles; people are the boss.

steps: Legislative power (making laws) belongs to the Congress of the Philippines (Article VI, Section 1).
Congress has two houses: the Senate and the House of Representatives.
The people also keep some lawmaking power through initiative and referendum.

wrong.The President: The President holds executive power (carrying out laws).
wrong.The Supreme Court: The Supreme Court holds judicial power (deciding cases).
wrong.The Senate only: The Senate is only one of the two houses of Congress.

350.tip: Make laws = Congress; enforce = President; interpret = courts.

steps: The Supreme Court has a Chief Justice and 14 Associate Justices (Article VIII, Section 4).
That makes 15 members in total.
It can sit en banc (all together) or in divisions of three, five or seven.

wrong.12: 12 is not the number of Associate Justices.
wrong.15: 15 is the total including the Chief Justice; the Associate Justices number 14.
wrong.9: 9 is the size of the US Supreme Court, not ours.

steps: Supreme Court Justices hold office until age 70 or until they become unable to do their work (Article VIII, Section 11).
Having no fixed term protects judges from political pressure.

wrong.65: 65 is not the retirement age for Justices.
wrong.75: 75 is not the retirement age for Justices.
wrong.60: 60 is not the retirement age for Justices.

steps: The House of Representatives has the exclusive power to initiate all impeachment cases (Article XI, Section 3).
The House acts like the prosecutor: it brings the charges.
The Senate then tries the case.

wrong.The Senate: The Senate tries and decides impeachment cases; it does not initiate them.
wrong.The Supreme Court: The Supreme Court has no role in starting impeachment.
wrong.The Ombudsman: The Ombudsman investigates officials, but it cannot start impeachment, and the Ombudsman can be impeached.

steps: The Senate has the sole power to try and decide impeachment cases (Article XI, Section 3).
The Senators act as the judges in the impeachment trial.

wrong.The House of Representatives: The House initiates impeachment; it does not try the case.
wrong.The Supreme Court: The Supreme Court does not try impeachment cases.
wrong.The Sandiganbayan: The Sandiganbayan is the anti-graft court that tries criminal cases against officials, not impeachment.

steps: Conviction needs two-thirds of all the Members of the Senate (Article XI, Section 3).
With 24 Senators, that means at least 16 votes.
The high number protects officials from being removed for purely political reasons.

wrong.A majority of all Senators: A simple majority is not enough to convict.
wrong.Three-fourths of all Senators: Three-fourths is not the required vote.
wrong.One-third of the House: One-third of all House Members is the vote needed to impeach (send the case to the Senate), not to convict.

355.tip: 1/3 of House to impeach, 2/3 of Senate to convict.

steps: Senators are NOT impeachable.
Impeachable officers (Article XI, Section 2): President, Vice President, Supreme Court Members, Constitutional Commission Members, and the Ombudsman.
A Senator can still be disciplined or expelled by the Senate itself.
356.tip: Impeachable: P, VP, SC, ConCom, Ombudsman. No legislators.

steps: The CSC has a Chairman and 2 Commissioners (Article IX-B, Section 1), so 3 members in all.
COA also has a Chairman and 2 Commissioners. COMELEC is bigger: a Chairman and 6 Commissioners.

wrong.4: The CSC does not have 4 Commissioners.
wrong.8: The CSC does not have 8 Commissioners.

steps: Under Article V, Section 1, you may vote if you are a Filipino citizen, at least 18, have lived in the Philippines at least 1 year and in your voting place at least 6 months before the election.
No literacy, property or similar requirement may be imposed, so the poor are not shut out of voting.

wrong.All residents regardless of citizenship: Only citizens may vote; foreigners living here cannot.
wrong.Citizens at least 18 years old who own p: The Constitution bans any property requirement for voting.

358.tip: Vote: Citizen, 18, 1 year PH, 6 months place.

steps: A people's initiative needs a petition signed by at least 12% of all registered voters (Article XVII, Section 2).
Every legislative district must also be represented by at least 3% of its registered voters.
This lets ordinary citizens propose changes to the Constitution, but only with wide support across the country.

wrong.3%: 3% is the minimum per legislative district, not the national total.
wrong.10%: 10% is not the national threshold for amending the Constitution.

steps: Article XVI, Section 1: the flag is red, white and blue, with a sun and three stars.
Blue for peace and justice, red for patriotism and valor, white triangle for equality.
The sun has 8 rays; the stars stand for Luzon, Visayas and Mindanao.

wrong.Red, yellow and blue: Yellow is the color of the sun and stars, but the flag's colors are red, white and blue.
wrong.Blue and white with a sun: This leaves out red and the three stars.
wrong.Red and blue with three stars only: This leaves out the white triangle and the sun.

steps: The Commission on Human Rights is created in Article XIII, Social Justice and Human Rights (Section 17).
It investigates human rights violations, especially those involving civil and political rights.
It is not one of the three Article IX Commissions.

wrong.Article III: Article III is the Bill of Rights, which lists rights but does not create the CHR.
wrong.Article IX: Article IX creates CSC, COMELEC and COA only.
wrong.Article XI: Article XI is Accountability of Public Officers (impeachment, Ombudsman).

361.tip: CHR = XIII (Human Rights is in the title of XIII).

steps: The civil service covers all government branches and agencies, including government-owned or controlled corporations (GOCCs) with original charters (Article IX-B, Section 2).
An original charter means the GOCC was created by a special law, like GSIS or SSS.
GOCCs formed under the general corporation law are not covered.

wrong.All private corporations: Private companies are not part of government, so they are outside the civil service.
wrong.Foreign embassies: Foreign embassies belong to other countries' governments.
wrong.Political parties: Political parties are private groups, not government agencies.

362.tip: GOCC with original charter = civil service.

steps: Civil servants may not engage, directly or indirectly, in electioneering or partisan political campaigns (Article IX-B, Section 2).
This keeps government service neutral, so citizens are served the same way whoever wins.
They may still vote; they just cannot campaign.

wrong.Religious activity: Freedom of religion is protected; civil servants may practice their faith.

363.tip: Government workers vote but do not campaign.

steps: The Civil Service Commission is the central personnel agency of government (Article IX-B, Section 3).
It handles hiring standards, exams (like this one), promotions and discipline of government workers.

wrong.Department of Labor and Employment: DOLE handles private-sector workers and labor issues.
wrong.Department of Budget and Management: DBM prepares and manages the national budget.

steps: Article XI, Section 12 calls the Ombudsman and his Deputies "protectors of the people".
They must act promptly on complaints against public officials and employees.

wrong.Guardians of the Constitution: This is a phrase often linked to the Supreme Court, not the Ombudsman.
wrong.Fiscalizers of Congress: This is not a constitutional title of the Ombudsman.
wrong.Keepers of the treasury: This is not a constitutional title of the Ombudsman.

steps: RA 6713, Section 5 requires officials to respond to letters and requests within 15 working days from receipt.
This prevents citizens from being ignored by government offices.

wrong.5: 5 working days is not the period set by RA 6713.
wrong.10: 10 working days is not the period set by RA 6713.
wrong.30: 30 days is the deadline for filing a SALN after assuming office, not for answering letters.

steps: Simple living is one of the eight norms of conduct in RA 6713, Section 4.
It means public servants should live modestly and not flaunt wealth, since they serve the people.
The other norms: commitment to public interest, professionalism, justness and sincerity, political neutrality, responsiveness to the public, nationalism and patriotism, commitment to democracy.

wrong.Seniority: Seniority is not one of the norms.
wrong.Party loyalty: The norm is political neutrality, the opposite of party loyalty.
wrong.Profit orientation: Public service is not about profit; the norm is commitment to public interest.

steps: Professionalism in RA 6713, Section 4 means doing your job with the highest degree of excellence, professionalism, intelligence and skill.
It is about how well you work, not whether you have a license.

wrong.Earn a professional license: Having a license is not what this norm means.
wrong.Work only during office hours: This is not the meaning of professionalism under RA 6713.
wrong.Avoid dealing with the public: Public servants should be responsive to the public, not avoid it.

steps: Political neutrality means serving everyone without unfair discrimination, regardless of party affiliation or preference (RA 6713, Section 4).
It ensures all citizens get the same service no matter whom they support.

wrong.Join the ruling party: Joining a party for favor goes against neutrality.
wrong.Avoid talking about the government: Neutrality does not mean silence about government.

369.tip: Neutral = same service for all parties.

steps: RA 6713, Section 7 prohibits soliciting or accepting gifts, favors or anything of monetary value in connection with official duties.
Gifts can create a sense of owing someone, which leads to unfair service.
This is one of the most common RA 6713 questions.

wrong.Filing a SALN: Filing a SALN is required by RA 6713, not prohibited.
wrong.Attending a seminar: Attending a seminar is a normal and allowed activity.
wrong.Answering letters promptly: RA 6713 actually requires answering letters within 15 working days.

steps: A new official must file the SALN within 30 days after assuming office (RA 6713, Section 8).
Then every year on or before April 30, and again within 30 days after leaving the service.
Filing at the start gives a baseline to compare later wealth against.

wrong.15: 15 working days is the period to answer letters, not to file the SALN.
wrong.60: 60 days is not the SALN deadline.
wrong.90: 90 days is not the SALN deadline.

371.tip: SALN: 30 days in, every April 30, 30 days out.

steps: Under RA 7080 (Anti-Plunder Act), as amended, plunder involves ill-gotten wealth of at least ₱50 million.
Plunder is a very serious crime of amassing huge amounts of stolen public money.
Smaller corrupt acts may fall under the Anti-Graft law (RA 3019) instead.

wrong.₱1 million: ₱1 million is too low; it is not the plunder threshold.
wrong.₱10 million: ₱10 million is not the plunder threshold.
wrong.₱100 million: ₱100 million is above the threshold; plunder starts at ₱50 million.

steps: Under RA 11032, highly technical applications must be acted on within 20 working days.
These involve detailed review, like technical evaluation or inspections.
Full set: simple 3, complex 7, highly technical 20 working days.

wrong.3: 3 working days is for simple transactions.
wrong.7: 7 working days is for complex transactions.
wrong.15: 15 working days is the RA 6713 deadline to answer letters, not an RA 11032 category.

steps: RA 11032 created the Anti-Red Tape Authority (ARTA).
ARTA implements the law, monitors compliance, and receives complaints about slow or difficult government services.
It is attached to the Office of the President.

wrong.Civil Service Commission: The CSC is the central personnel agency; it was not created by RA 11032.
wrong.Department of Trade and Industry: DTI handles trade and business but is not the agency created by RA 11032.
wrong.Office of the Ombudsman: The Ombudsman investigates officials; it was created by the Constitution, not RA 11032.

374.tip: Anti-Red Tape Act -> Anti-Red Tape Authority.

steps: The Data Privacy Act (RA 10173) created the National Privacy Commission (NPC).
The NPC enforces the law, handles complaints, and checks that personal data is handled properly.

wrong.Department of Information and Communicat: DICT handles ICT policy and programs but is not the agency that administers the Data Privacy Act.
wrong.National Bureau of Investigation: The NBI investigates crimes but does not administer the Data Privacy Act.
wrong.Securities and Exchange Commission: The SEC regulates corporations and securities.

steps: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights has 30 articles.
They cover civil, political, economic, social and cultural rights.

wrong.10: 10 is not the number of UDHR articles; December 10 is Human Rights Day.
wrong.25: 25 is not the number of UDHR articles.
wrong.45: 45 is not the number of UDHR articles.

steps: Civil and political rights are called first-generation rights.
Examples: free speech, voting, fair trial, freedom of religion.
They mainly protect individuals from government abuse.

wrong.Second-generation rights: Second-generation rights are economic, social and cultural rights (education, work).
wrong.Third-generation rights: Third-generation rights are solidarity rights (development, healthy environment).
wrong.Collective rights: Collective rights belong to groups, like peoples or communities.

steps: Education, work and social security are economic, social and cultural rights.
These are second-generation rights.
They usually need the government to act and provide, like building schools.

wrong.Civil rights: Civil rights include free speech and fair trial.
wrong.Solidarity rights: Solidarity rights are third-generation, like the right to development.
wrong.Political rights: Political rights include voting and running for office.

steps: The right to development and the right to a healthy environment are third-generation (solidarity) rights.
They belong to communities and peoples, not just individuals.
They need cooperation among nations to achieve.

wrong.First-generation rights: First-generation rights are civil and political.
wrong.Second-generation rights: Second-generation rights are economic, social and cultural.
wrong.Political rights: Political rights are part of the first generation.

379.tip: 3rd generation = shared rights for everyone together.

steps: Universal means human rights belong to everyone, everywhere.
Race, sex, religion or nationality do not matter.

wrong.Inalienable: Inalienable means they cannot be taken away or given up.
wrong.Absolute: Many rights can be lawfully limited, so they are not absolute.

380.tip: Universal = for the whole universe of people.

steps: Interdependent and indivisible means rights depend on one another.
Example: without education, it is hard to exercise free speech and voting well.
Violating one right often harms others.

wrong.Universal: Universal means they belong to everyone.
wrong.Relative: Relative is not a characteristic of human rights.

381.tip: Rights are a package: one affects all.

steps: Negative peace is simply the absence of war or direct violence.
Positive peace goes further: justice, fairness and the removal of structural violence.
These terms come from peace studies (Johan Galtung).

wrong.Positive peace: Positive peace needs justice and fairness, not just no war.
wrong.Structural peace: This is not the standard term for the absence of violence.
wrong.Cultural peace: This is not the standard term for the absence of violence.

382.tip: Negative = no war yet; positive = real justice.

steps: Structural violence is harm caused by unfair social systems, not a single attacker.
Examples: poverty, hunger, discrimination built into how society works.
It harms people slowly, often unseen.

wrong.Direct violence: Direct violence is physical harm done by one person or group, like hitting or shooting.
wrong.Physical violence: Physical violence is bodily harm, a type of direct violence.
wrong.Domestic violence: Domestic violence happens within the home or family.

steps: International humanitarian law (IHL) is the set of rules that protects people during armed conflict.
It protects civilians, the wounded, the sick and prisoners of war.
Also called the law of war or law of armed conflict.

wrong.Civil law: Civil law deals with private relations like property and contracts.
wrong.Labor law: Labor law deals with workers and employers.

steps: The four Geneva Conventions were adopted in 1949, after World War II.
They form the core of international humanitarian law.

wrong.1919: 1919 is the year of the Treaty of Versailles after World War I.
wrong.1945: 1945 is the founding year of the United Nations.
wrong.1966: 1966 is the year the two International Covenants on human rights were adopted.

steps: Human Rights Day is December 10.
It marks the adoption of the UDHR on December 10, 1948.
RA 9003 requires a Materials Recovery Facility (MRF) in every barangay or cluster of barangays.
An MRF receives, sorts and recovers recyclable and compostable waste.
It reduces what goes to disposal sites.

wrong.Sanitary landfill: A sanitary landfill is a final disposal site, usually run at the city or municipal level, not per barangay.
wrong.Incinerator: Incineration that gives off toxic fumes is banned by the Clean Air Act.
wrong.Water treatment plant: Water treatment is related to the Clean Water Act, not RA 9003.

steps: RA 9003 prohibits open dumping of garbage.
Open dumps pollute soil, water and air, and spread disease.
The law promotes segregation, recycling and composting instead.

wrong.Segregation at source: Segregation at source is required by RA 9003.

388.tip: RA 9003: segregate, recycle, compost; no open dumps.

steps: The Clean Air Act (RA 8749) bans incineration of municipal, biomedical and hazardous waste that emits poisonous and toxic fumes.
Burning trash releases harmful chemicals into the air we breathe.

wrong.Sanitary landfilling: Sanitary landfills are an allowed disposal method under RA 9003.

389.tip: Clean Air Act: no toxic burning.

steps: The Montreal Protocol (1987) phases out ozone-depleting substances like CFCs.
The ozone layer protects us from harmful ultraviolet rays.

wrong.Kyoto Protocol: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) set greenhouse gas reduction targets.
wrong.Paris Agreement: The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to limit global warming.
wrong.Basel Convention: The Basel Convention controls the movement of hazardous waste across borders.

steps: The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to keep global warming well below 2°C, and to pursue efforts to limit it to 1.5°C.
It is under the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change.

wrong.Kyoto Protocol: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) is an older climate treaty.
wrong.Montreal Protocol: The Montreal Protocol (1987) protects the ozone layer.
wrong.Rio Declaration: The Rio Declaration (1992) set principles on environment and development.

steps: Sustainable development meets present needs without compromising future generations' ability to meet theirs.
This definition comes from the Brundtland Report (1987).
It balances economic growth, social welfare and environmental protection.

wrong.Industrialization: Industrialization is growth of factories and industry.
wrong.Urbanization: Urbanization is the growth of cities.
wrong.Globalization: Globalization is the increasing connection of countries.

392.tip: Sustainable = enough for now, enough for later.

steps: Gases that trap heat in the atmosphere, like carbon dioxide and methane, are greenhouse gases.
They act like the glass of a greenhouse, warming the Earth.
Too much of them causes global warming and climate change.

wrong.Noble gases: Noble gases (helium, neon, argon) are unreactive elements in chemistry.
wrong.Ozone gases: Ozone is a single gas that forms the ozone layer; carbon dioxide and methane are not ozone.
wrong.Inert gases: Inert gases is another name for noble gases.

steps: Earth Day is observed every April 22.
It is a day to raise awareness about protecting the environment.
World Environment Day is June 5.
It is the UN's day for environmental awareness and action.

wrong.September 16: September 16 is the International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer.

steps: The three Rs are Reduce, Reuse, Recycle.
Reduce means using less; reuse means using items again; recycle means turning waste into new materials.
Reducing waste first is the best option.

wrong.Remove, reuse, refuse: This is not the standard three Rs.
wrong.Reduce, recover, reject: This is not the standard three Rs.
wrong.Repair, return, remove: This is not the standard three Rs.

396.tip: Reduce first, then reuse, then recycle.

steps: RA 9729, the Climate Change Act of 2009, created the Climate Change Commission.
The Commission coordinates climate change policies and programs of the government.

wrong.RA 9003: RA 9003 is the Ecological Solid Waste Management Act of 2000.
wrong.RA 8749: RA 8749 is the Philippine Clean Air Act of 1999.
wrong.RA 10121: RA 10121 is the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act of 2010, which created the NDRRMC.
